messages:
maria: Quick design thread — want feedback on the compact 'Preview recipients' mini-panel for the SLO notification flow. I pushed two variants in Figma: a stacked list vs. a condensed pill row. Which is clearer when there are 6+ channels?

sam: Stacked list is clearer for discovery but eats vertical real estate on the alert rule page. The pill row feels cleaner but might hide overflow. Can we show a collapse/expand when >3? :thinking_face:

jonathan: Agree re collapse. Also consider keyboard access: pills need focus styles and arrow-key traversal, otherwise screen readers announce them oddly. Elaine — any a11y concerns with a collapsible row?

elaine: Collapsible is fine if we implement proper aria-controls + aria-expanded on the toggle and ensure the collapsed state is still reachable via keyboard. For the pill row, add role="list" and role="listitem" on channel chips and provide an accessible label like "Preview recipients: 4 items". Also ensure color contrast on status badges.

luis: One more UX nit: when suppression rules are active, we should visually indicate which channels are suppressed in the preview (gray out + tooltip). Right now the comps don't show suppression at all. That causes false confidence when users click Preview.

maria: Good point. Proposal: show small muted icon on suppressed channels + hover tooltip "Suppressed by schedule: weekdays 9-17". For the pill row collapsed view, show "+2 suppressed" as a chip. Thoughts?

sam: Love the +2 suppressed chip. Keeps the surface tidy and communicates state. For copy, prefer "Suppressed" vs "Muted" to match backend naming (we use suppression elsewhere).

jonathan: Technical: for preview generation we currently call the preview API synchronously which can add ~300ms. If we add hover tooltips for each pill that trigger requests, we'll need to debounce and cache per-rule. Or we can materialize the suppression mapping in the initial preview payload. Which is better?

maria: Let's avoid extra round trips on hover. Jonathan — can you include suppression mapping in the preview payload? Even if it's a small extra payload, it keeps interactions snappy.

jonathan: Yep, I'll add suppressed_channels[] to the preview response. Will also return a short reason string so the tooltip text is localizable. API change should be backward compatible.

elaine: For the dialog that opens the full preview: ensure role=dialog, focus trap, and set aria-describedby to the explanation paragraph. Also make the close button accessible via label "Close preview". Keyboard screenshots look fine.

maria: Copy question — inside the preview, we show a header: "Notification preview" vs "Who will be notified". Which is clearer for end users?

sam: "Who will be notified" reads more directly. "Notification preview" sounds like the message content preview. So I'd vote for the explicit phrasing.

luis: Small UX edge case: if a channel is disabled in the user's org (no integration), we should surface a warning line and exclude it from the count. Otherwise preview counts are off. Add a muted warning icon in the pill and exclude it from actionable recipients.

maria: Good catch. We'll add a small inline legend: green = active, gray = suppressed, red-outline = disabled/misconfigured. Elaine, confirm those color semantics are ok for contrast.

elaine: Red-outline is fine as long as the outline thickness and focus ring meet AA. Provide alternative text in the tooltip like "Email integration misconfigured" so screen reader users get the same info.

design-bot: New Figma frames uploaded: 
- compact-pills-v1 (collapsed + expanded states)
- stacked-list-v2 (with suppression/disabled states)
Link: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/notify-preview-compacts

maria: Next steps: Jonathan to add suppression mapping to preview API and return a small reason string. Design to iterate on pill overflow behavior (show +N) and add legend. Elaine will run keyboard + screen reader pass once dev builds a prototype. Sam will update copy to "Who will be notified". Please reply here when tasks are started. :rocket:
